summary: encodeURIComponent percent-encodes a string as a URI component using UTF-8.
documentation: encodeURIComponent percent-encodes a string as a URI component using UTF-8. Reserved URL separators such as slash, question mark and ampersand are encoded, so the result can represent one value rather than changing URL structure.
inputs: A well-formed Unicode string, with no lone surrogate code units.
caution: This encodes a component rather than a complete URL. It is not HTML escaping, encryption or validation of a destination; spaces become %20 rather than the plus used by some form encodings.
scenarios: Encode one search value when constructing a documented URL.
Represent a filename as one path segment.
Preserve ampersands inside a filter value instead of starting another parameter.
title: Encode one URL component
problem: Return encodeURIComponent(input). Encode reserved separators and spaces, keep JavaScript’s standard unescaped component characters, and support well-formed Unicode. Do not encode an entire assembled URL.
hint: Apply the global encodeURIComponent function once to the raw value.
goal: Use encodeURIComponent() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
